name: Midnight Purple
lede: Midnight Purple is a near-black purple from a 2010 online color survey, named for the dark of night and barely distinguishable on screen from Deep Purple.

sections.title: A time-of-day word
sections.body:
The ColorHub library files Midnight Purple as a nature-tier name, built on the time-of-day word *midnight* the way [[mud-green|Mud Green]] and [[milk-chocolate|Milk Chocolate]] are built on *mud* and *milk* [1]. Its only recorded source is the xkcd 2010 crowd color survey; no earlier record turns up in our data, so who first paired the word with this exact hex is undocumented [1]. At hex #280137 it measures lightness 7 and chroma 39 in LCH, among the darkest, most saturated entries in the library [1].

At that darkness hue differences compress. Midnight Purple sits 3.1 CIEDE2000 units from [[deep-purple|Deep Purple]], our graph's threshold for an almost-identical screen color, and the library separately logs Very Dark Purple as a near-duplicate crowd name only 1.3 units away [1][2]. [[aubergine|Aubergine]] is the nearest match in the app's own curriculum, 6.9 units off, and [[russian-violet|Russian Violet]] sits 5.8 units away, reading lighter [1][2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive has a color this dark and this saturated covering even 1% of its canvas, as photographed [3]. That is a gap in this archive's holdings, not a claim that painters never mixed a purple this deep [3].
